title: ServiceNow’s AI-Powered Flow Service Desk Aims To Open Midmarket Opportunities
key_facts: ServiceNow introduced Flow by ServiceNow on Thursday (1 Oct 2026): a stand-alone, AI-powered, conversational IT service desk built for quick setup in midsize businesses.
CRN calls it ServiceNow's first AI-native product aimed at the "Fortune 500,000", the mid-range and commercial market that CEO Bill McDermott hinted at in July.
It works inside Slack and Microsoft Teams; Jeff Hausman, ServiceNow executive vice president, says it can be running within minutes or hours.
Existing customers can sync Flow back to the core ServiceNow platform; new customers can run it without the core platform.
Pricing is consumption-based, using Now Assist packs or credits; ServiceNow is still working out how to charge new customers who do not use Now Assist.
Flow is due for existing customers in North America from 6 Oct 2026, and for all existing and new customers worldwide later in the fourth calendar quarter.
It first targets internal employee requests; Hausman says it could later extend to external users.
Partner Ahead's Ryan Crosby welcomes the move away from ServiceNow's traditional seat-based licences; ServiceNow's Michael Park says Flow opens segments the company could not reach before.
quote_evidence: Flow by ServiceNow is slated to be available for existing customers in North America starting Oct. 6, and then for all existing and new customers worldwide later in the fourth calendar quarter, Hausman said.
Pricing is consumption-based based on the usage of ServiceNow’s Now Assist packs or Now Assist credits, Hausman said.
Flow by ServiceNow is a very quick and easily deployed technology that can be set up and running within minutes or hours, Hausman said.
why_it_matters_hint: ServiceNow, which mainly sells to large companies, is reaching for midsize firms and giving its partner companies a new product to sell.
event_date: Thursday 1 Oct 2026 (CRN: 'ServiceNow Thursday introduced'); CRN published 2 Oct 2026.
notes: Interviews with ServiceNow executives and one partner; speed-of-setup and market claims are company statements, not independent tests. CRN is a trade outlet for IT resellers.
